title: Puppy 'stolen' from Austin shelter may be returned 'no questions asked,' staff says - NewsBreak
text:
By Margaret Grigsby ,
6 hours ago
AUSTIN (KXAN) — The Austin Human Society said it is looking for a pup named Chico that went missing after a visit with a potential adopter.
AHS released video of a woman who came to the shelter around 5:30 p.m. Tuesday, April 7, and expressed interest in adopting Chico, according to staff.
The woman filled out an adoption application and the shelter staff said they gave her “basic information” about the pup. The staff then brought out Chico for a meet-and-greet with his potential adopter.
Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) That’s the last time shelter staff report seeing the dog.
“Shortly after being set up in a visitation room to meet the puppy, she put Chico in her purse and quickly left the facility,” AHS said in a press release Thursday.
Shelter workers said they tried to contact the woman through information she wrote on her application, but the efforts have “been a dead end.”
Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) “Staff did not realize she had left with the puppy for a few minutes, but security cameras caught her leaving the facility out of a volunteer/staff only entrance,” AHS added.
Chico is a four-month-old, black and brown wire-haired terrier mix weighing seven pounds. He was only at the shelter for a day and was scheduled for neuter surgery soon, shelter staff said. Chico had a round of vaccines, but needs an additional round before he’s considered fully vaccinated.
Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) Austin Human Society says woman took puppy named Chico during adoption visit April 7, 2026. (Austin Humane Society photo) Chico has a microchip, and AHS has reported Chico as “stolen” to the microchip company and Austin Police.
KXAN asked the Austin Humane Society for an APD police report number associated with their case. Shelter staff said they were waiting for “additional guidance” from police before they could provide additional details.
The Austin Police Department said it did not have a record of a reported theft at AHS’s address. This story will be updated if additional information about the case becomes available.
Anyone with information about the whereabouts of Chico or knows about his disappearance from the Austin Humane Society, located at 124 W Anderson Ln. in north Austin, is asked to send a message to media@austinhumanesociety.org or call 512-646-7387 .
AHS said Chico may be returned — no questions asked — directly to the shelter any time from 8 a.m. – 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday, or 8 a.m. – 5 p.m. Sunday.
